bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42510080 (elfutils): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz-libelf [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42510080
bug_description.normalized:
The saved MemorySanitizer stack crashes in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82`, so the witness follows the second `fuzz_logic_one(filename, 1)` pass. In that pass, libelf reads 8 section headers at fixed 64-byte strides from `e_shoff = 0`. Section 3 is the section-header string table (`SHT_STRTAB`, `sh_offset = 0x200`, `sh_size = 0x60`) but its header also carries `SHF_COMPRESSED`. The harness therefore reaches `elf_compress(scn, 1, 0)` on section 3 before any later section names are tested. Inside `elf_compress()`, `compressed = (sh_flags & SHF_COMPRESSED)` becomes `0x800`, so the buggy check `if (compressed == 1)` does not reject the already-compressed section. `__libelf_compress()` then asks `elf_getdata()` for section 3, which classifies it as `ELF_T_CHDR`, reads the 96 bytes at file offset `0x200`, and uses the special `Elf64_cvt_chdr()` helper that `memmove`s the whole buffer while converting only the first 24-byte header. That lets libelf recompress the complete 96-byte string-table image into a valid in-memory compressed section and later inflate it successfully through `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)`, yielding a name that starts with `.z`. Section 4 still has the out-of-range name offset `0x20202020`, so section 5 becomes the first later non-`SHF_COMPRESSED` section whose `.z*` name reaches `elf_compress_gnu()`.

For section 5, `__libelf_set_rawdata_wrlock()` copies `sh_offset = 32`, `sh_size = 28`, `sh_type = 0x6ffffffa (SHT_SUNW_move)`, and `sh_addralign = 0xffffffff20202020` from the header at file offset `0x140`. The admission logic maps `SHT_SUNW_move` to `ELF_T_MOVE` and accepts `sh_size = 28` because `__libelf_type_sizes[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_MOVE]` is the 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` layout from `exttypes.h`. Because the file is big-endian on the saved little-endian x86_64 build, `convert_data()` must take the structured xlate path, allocate a 28-byte heap buffer, and dispatch `__elf_xfctstom[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_MOVE] = Elf64_cvt_Move`. That converter is generated from the shared `START / END` macro in `libelf/gelf_xlate.c`, but it iterates in units of the native in-memory `Elf64_Move` size. On the saved build `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32, so with `len = 28` the loop count is zero and the vulnerable macro performs no writes and no fallback copy. `convert_data()` publishes that untouched heap allocation as `data->d_buf`, and `elf_compress_gnu()` then evaluates `data->d_size < 12 || memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4) != 0)`; because `data->d_size` is 28, `memcmp` reads bytes `data->d_buf[0..3]` while they are still uninitialized, producing the saved MSAN report. The fix adds `size_t sz` plus `if (len % sz > 0) memmove(dest, src, len % sz);`; for this exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch that copies all 28 bytes and removes the undefined read.

source.description: First project-level materialization on the crashing second-pass reachability chain. When `elf_getdata()` is pulled on section 3 during `elf_compress(scn, 1, 0)`, libelf copies the malformed shstrtab header fields into locals that decide where the 96-byte table is read from and how it is typed.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is parsed with libelf's fixed 64-byte section-header size because `file_read_elf()` uses `e_shoff = 0` and `e_shnum = 8`, not the bogus on-disk `e_shentsize`. The saved crash is on `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82`, so the relevant call is the second `fuzz_logic_one(filename, 1)` pass. Before section 5 is named, section 3's header at file offset `0xc0` supplies `sh_offset = 0x200`, `sh_size = 0x60`, `sh_type = SHT_STRTAB`, `sh_addralign = 0x2000000000000000`, and `sh_flags = 0x202020202020ff20` to this statement.

sink.description: MSAN sink. This GNU-header check reaches `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)`, which reads the first four bytes of the translated section-5 buffer after `convert_data()` published a 28-byte heap buffer that `Elf64_cvt_Move` left untouched.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` place the top project frame at `libelf/elf_compress_gnu.c:155` in `elf_compress_gnu()` with the crash summarized as `MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value in memcmp`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The shared xlate macro iterates in units of the native `Elf64_Move` size, but this witness was admitted as a single 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` record. For the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch reached here, `len` is 28 and `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32 on the saved x86_64 build, so the loop count is zero and the vulnerable converter returns without writing any bytes to the freshly allocated destination buffer.
root_cause.note: The selected dispatch arm is exact: `__elf_xfctstom[ELFCLASS64 - 1][ELF_T_MOVE] = Elf64_cvt_Move`. `patch.diff` adds `size_t sz` and `if (len % sz > 0) memmove (dest, src, len % sz);` after this loop; for this witness `len % sz` is 28, so the patched converter copies the whole buffer even though `n` is 0.

parser_admitted.description: The saved MSAN stack points to `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82`, the second `fuzz_logic_one(filename, 1)` pass. In that pass, section 3 is the shstrtab (`SHT_STRTAB`, `sh_offset = 0x200`, `sh_size = 0x60`) and also has `SHF_COMPRESSED`, so the harness first runs `elf_compress(scn, 1, 0)` on section 3. That in-memory recompression makes later `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)` return the `.z...` string at the start of the table; section 4 still has the out-of-range name offset `0x20202020`, so section 5 with `sh_name = 0` is the first later non-`SHF_COMPRESSED` section that reaches `elf_compress_gnu()`.

coarse_trace.summary: In the crashing second `fuzz_logic_one(filename, 1)` pass, section 3 is treated as a compressed shstrtab; `elf_compress(scn, 1, 0)` wrongly recompresses that already-`SHF_COMPRESSED` section into a valid in-memory compressed string table, and later `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)` yields the `.z...` name that selects section 5.

For section 5, libelf copies the header values, accepts `sh_size = 28` as one external `Elf64_Ext_Move`, reads the 28 section bytes from file offset `0x20`, records `scn->rawdata.d.d_type = ELF_T_MOVE`, and enters `convert_data()`'s structured xlate path.

The exact dispatch arm is `Elf64_cvt_Move`, and its vulnerable loop counts in 32-byte native `Elf64_Move` records, so a 28-byte input yields zero iterations and no fallback copy, leaving the whole destination buffer uninitialized.

The untouched 28-byte `Elf_Data` buffer is published as `data->d_buf`, and `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)` reads bytes `0..3` from that uninitialized heap allocation, triggering the saved MemorySanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: Harness checkpoint for the saved crashing pass. The MSAN stack ends at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82`, which is the second `fuzz_logic_one(filename, 1)` call. On that pass, section 3 is reached before section 5, its `sh_flags = 0x202020202020ff20` set `SHF_COMPRESSED`, and the harness therefore calls `elf_compress(scn, 1, 0)` on the shstrtab before any later section names are tested.

For section 3, `sh_flags & SHF_COMPRESSED` is `0x800`, so the buggy test `compressed == 1` is false and the already-compressed shstrtab is recompressed instead of being rejected as `ELF_E_ALREADY_COMPRESSED`.

fine_trace.note: Source. When `__libelf_compress()` asks for section 3 data, libelf materializes the malformed shstrtab header fields `offset = 0x200`, `size = 0x60`, `type = SHT_STRTAB`, `align = 0x2000000000000000`, and `flags = 0x202020202020ff20` from the section header at file offset `0xc0`.

Because section 3 still carries `SHF_COMPRESSED`, libelf reclassifies its bytes as `ELF_T_CHDR` rather than plain string-table bytes. That exact type choice selects the special `Elf64_cvt_chdr()` helper for the later `elf_getdata()` conversion.

fine_trace.code: if (dest != src) memmove (dest, src, len); if (len >= sizeof (Elf64_Chdr)) Elf64_cvt_Chdr (dest, src, sizeof (Elf64_Chdr), encode);
fine_trace.note: The `ELF_T_CHDR` converter is special: it copies all `len` bytes and only byte-swaps the first 24-byte header. For section 3, that means `elf_getdata()` hands `__libelf_compress()` the entire 96-byte byte image, preserving the leading `.z` bytes and the trailing NUL terminator instead of dropping the payload after the header.

fine_trace.code: chdr.ch_type = ELFCOMPRESS_ZLIB; chdr.ch_reserved = 0; chdr.ch_size = orig_size; chdr.ch_addralign = sh_addralign; ... __libelf_reset_rawdata (scn, out_buf, new_size, 1, ELF_T_CHDR);
fine_trace.note: libelf compresses the full 96-byte section-3 image from step 5, prepends a valid `Elf64_Chdr` with `ch_type = ELFCOMPRESS_ZLIB` and `ch_size = 96`, and replaces section 3's rawdata with that self-consistent compressed buffer. `__libelf_reset_rawdata()` immediately rebuilds the data list through `Elf64_cvt_chdr()`, so the new zlib payload is preserved in memory together with the header.

When section 5 later calls `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)`, section 3 is now a valid compressed section. `get_zdata()` therefore inflates the step-6 buffer back into a 96-byte `zdata_base` that matches the original shstrtab bytes from file offset `0x200`.

For section 5, `sh_name = 0`, so `elf_strptr(elf, 3, 0)` returns `&strscn->zdata_base[0]`, whose first bytes are `.z`. Section 4 still has `sh_name = 0x20202020`, which stays out of range for the 96-byte table, and section 5's own `sh_flags = 0x2020202020202020` leave the earlier `SHF_COMPRESSED` branch untaken. Section 5 is therefore the first later section whose name test reaches `elf_compress_gnu()`.

This fast-path predicate is false on the witness. The file is big-endian (`EI_DATA = ELFDATA2MSB`), the saved x86_64 build uses `MY_ELFDATA = ELFDATA2LSB`, and step 12 stored `type = ELF_T_MOVE`, so `convert_data()` must take the structured xlate branch instead of the raw-byte copy/alias path.

MSAN allocation origin. `convert_data()` allocates a fresh 28-byte destination buffer for the translated section-5 data, and `malloc` leaves all 28 bytes uninitialized until a later write defines them.

Root cause. `Elf64_cvt_Move` counts in units of the native `Elf64_Move` type, not the 28-byte external `Elf64_Ext_Move` that step 10 used for admission. On the saved x86_64 build `sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32, so with `len = 28` the loop computes `n = 0`, executes zero iterations, and this vulnerable revision has no fallback `memmove`; none of `dest[0..27]` are written.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the shared xlate macro in `libelf/gelf_xlate.c` to compute `sz` and copy any `len % sz` remainder with `memmove`. For the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` dispatch on this witness, `len` is 28 and `sz = sizeof (Elf64_Move)` is 32, so the patched fallback copies all 28 bytes and prevents the later `memcmp` at fine-trace step 18 from reading poison.

MSAN attributes the poison to the heap allocation at `convert_data:168` (fine-trace step 14), and fine-trace steps 15 through 17 show the exact `Elf64_cvt_Move` path where `len = 28` yields zero loop iterations and leaves that allocation wholly uninitialized before step 18 consumes it.

The saved crash stack `memcmp -> elf_compress_gnu -> fuzz_logic_one -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the second-pass section-selection checkpoint in steps 0 through 8 and the sink in step 18, while the allocation stack `convert_data -> __libelf_set_data_list_rdlock -> __elf_getdata_rdlock -> elf_getdata -> elf_compress_gnu` is reflected by steps 13 through 18.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Steps 0 through 8 repair section 3 into a valid in-memory shstrtab and make section 5 selectable; step 9 imports section 5's header fields, step 10 admits `sh_size = 28` as one external `Elf64_Ext_Move`, step 11 loads the 28 section bytes, step 12 stores `ELF_T_MOVE`, step 13 forces structured xlate, step 14 allocates the destination, step 15 resolves `Elf64_cvt_Move`, step 16 leaves all 28 bytes undefined, step 17 publishes that buffer as `data->d_buf`, and step 18 reads bytes `0..3` in `memcmp`.

format.name: Exact staged 608-byte ELF witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 608-byte file at `gt_results/arvo_42510080/poc`; no broader input class is claimed. In the saved crashing second pass (`LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput:82`), the file must preserve libelf's fixed `e_shoff = 0`, `e_shnum = 8` section-header layout, section 3 as `SHT_STRTAB` with `sh_offset = 0x200`, `sh_size = 0x60`, and `SHF_COMPRESSED` set, and section 5 as a non-`SHF_COMPRESSED` `SHT_SUNW_move` section with `sh_name = 0`, `sh_offset = 0x20`, and `sh_size = 0x1c`. That exact combination lets section 3 be recompressed into a valid in-memory shstrtab before section 5 is named, then drives section 5 into the `Elf64_cvt_Move` zero-iteration case before `memcmp(data->d_buf, "ZLIB", 4)`.
